title: Spectral gaps of ironed two-qubit gadgets matching the iSWAP gap
abstract: We prove that every ironed two-qubit gadget whose KAK-derived parameter satisfies $a=5/9$ has, on the complete graph $K_n$ with $n\geqslant 5$, the same second-moment spectral gap as the iSWAP gadget. The central step is a representation-theoretic localisation theorem: the largest strictly negative eigenvalue of the associated $\mathfrak S_n$-invariant operator always occurs in the highest-spin $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ summand. A local positive-semidefinite decomposition separates every spin sector except the two highest. This settles a conjecture of Kong, Li, and Liu.
summary: The authors prove that a specific family of two-qubit quantum gadgets achieves the same spectral gap as the iSWAP gadget when implemented on large complete graphs. They achieve this by employing advanced techniques from representation theory and analyzing the eigenvalues of associated moment operators across different spin sectors.
main_problem: The paper proves that a specific class of two-qubit quantum circuits (ironed gadgets) exhibits the same spectral gap as the well-known iSWAP gadget when operating on large complete graphs.
main_result: For the condition $a=5/9$ and $n \ge 5$, the second-moment spectral gap of the ironed two-qubit gadget matches that of the iSWAP gadget, settling a prior conjecture.
method: The analysis heavily relies on representation theory (Schur–Weyl duality) to decompose large moment operators into independent spin sectors and then uses properties of tridiagonal Jacobi matrices to bound eigenvalues.
model_or_system: The system involves 'ironed two-qubit gadgets' modeled by second-moment operators ($T_{IG}^{2,K_n}$) acting on $V^{\otimes n}$ over the complete graph $K_n$. The comparison benchmark is the iSWAP gadget.
key_observables: The primary observable is the second-moment spectral gap, $\Delta(T) = 1 - \max(\lambda^*(T), |\lambda_{\min}(T)|)$.
important_parameters: The critical parameter condition is $a=5/9$, and the graph size must satisfy $n \ge 5$.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on a representation-theoretic localization theorem showing that the most negative eigenvalue resides in the highest-spin $	ext{SU}(2)$ summand, allowing for sector-by-sector analysis.

paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the moment operators on $K_n$, decomposing them using Schur–Weyl duality into spin sectors. It then proves a localization theorem (Theorem 1.2) that restricts the gap determination to the highest-spin sector, culminating in proving the equality of spectral gaps (Theorem 5.4).
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical proof regarding the performance scaling of quantum circuits used for quantum information tasks, connecting abstract algebraic structures (representation theory) to concrete physical measures like spectral gaps.
